# The progress points

The contract between 53ef07aa's run log (dc) and eae7633d's toasts (ic). dc writes this file and ic agrees to it before either side codes. After that, neither changes a point without the other.

ic agreed on 23 Nov 2026 with four changes, all taken here: the step's timing (rule 2), a move's frame, three fields on `finished`, and `run` on every point. ic's reasons are in `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-ic/arngz-toasts/points-reply.md` (sha256 ed1e7a2ee233).

ST6d8eed9 (hv decisions 23 and 26) changes the points on cc's word and ic's: apply launches no app (WP 35219619), a reload and one retry after Hammerspoon's window filter fails (WP a45b3aeb, rule 10), and a pause when the pointer moves (WP 4cb617e2, rule 11).

## The points

Every point carries `run`, the CLI's run id, besides the fields below.

| Point      | When                                                                                   | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Verbs             |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `start`    | The engine has the request and begins                                                  | `verb`, `desk` (empty for which, discover and doctor), `after_reload_of` (on the retry after a reload, the run's id, which is the retry's own `run`; absent otherwise; rule 10)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | every engine verb |
| `observed` | The displays, their desktops and the windows have been read                            | `displays`, `desktops`, `windows` (named), `order` ("record" when every display's order is com.apple.spaces', else eg "of 3 displays: live on 1, unread on 1", naming only the counts that are not 0, and "no displays" when there are none; WP 93ea7f8a), `visitors` (desktops filed under another display)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | every engine verb |
| `planned`  | The plan is made, or refused                                                           | `creates`, `moves`, `places`, `nothing` (true when there is nothing to do), `refused` (the words, when it refused)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | apply, diff       |
| `waiting`  | A wait begins                                                                          | `for` ("the displays to settle", "new desktops", "unseen windows", "the pointer to be still"), `seconds` (its longest), `still` (for the pointer alone: how many seconds it must stay still; rule 11)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | apply             |
| `step`     | Before each create, move, place or recheck (rule 2), and again after a pause (rule 11) | `i`, `n`, `kind`, `app`, `display` (the desk's name for it), `desktop` (its ordinal); for a move, also the window's frame now as `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, and `via` (for a move that goes round through another display, the desk's name for it, or the screen's name when the desk does not describe it)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | apply             |
| `finished` | The run has its answer, whatever it is                                                 | `outcome` ("done", "partly", "refused" or "failed"), `exit`, `placed`, `in_place` (entries that needed nothing), `failed`, `unseen`, `not_running` (entries whose app is not running, which apply never launches), `not_running_apps` (those apps' names as one string, eg "Teams, Slack"; absent when every app ran), `created` (desktops added), `seconds`, `first` (the words of the first counted entry not placed, or of a refusal or a failed run), `first_outcome` ("failed" or "unseen": what the entry first names was, in the tally's own keys, since a not-running entry is uncounted and never first; absent when first is a refusal's or a failed run's words), `fix` (a refusal's fix, or that entry's), `log` (the log's path), `reload` (true when the CLI is to reload Hammerspoon's config and run the verb again: a refusal of kind reload, or an apply that ran and asks for it; rule 10), `paused` (how many times the run paused for the pointer, 0 when it did not; rule 11) | every engine verb |

## Rules

1. **Order.** Each run emits `start` once. Then, for apply, one `waiting` for "the displays to settle" when they have not been quiet for 5 s, counted from the later of the display watcher's last change and its start (WP 93ea7f8a's settle; agreed by ic on 23 Nov 2026: the toast shows it as is). Then `observed`, then for apply and diff `planned`, then any number of `waiting` and `step`, then `finished` once. auto's which and discover --save wait for the same quiet before they run: each `unsettled` answer the engine gives while they wait sends no point, and the run's `start` comes with the ask that reads.
2. **A step goes out before its work.** Hammerspoon draws only when its run loop turns, and the engine holds the loop inside each callback. So each `step` is emitted in the callback before the one that does it: run_phase emits it before scheduling that callback. For organise, that is step i before the callback for op i is scheduled. prepare runs all its creates in one callback, so their steps all go out before that callback, and the toast shows the batch's last step while the batch runs. That was dc's choice of ic's two options, because it leaves apply's phases as they are.
3. **`finished` always comes.** It comes after a refusal, after a Lua error in a phase, and on the guarded path that answers a crashed apply, so no toast is left at Running. Nothing follows it. A second apply refused while one runs emits its own `start` and `finished`, under its own `run`, so its toast leaves the running one alone.
4. **Plain values.** A point's fields are strings, numbers and booleans. The log holds the windows and the desktop lists, and the toasts never need them.
5. **One emitter, two listeners.** The engine emits each point once. The log writes it as a record, and the toast hook receives the same name and fields. The hook is `opt/arngz/lib/toast.lua`, which returns a table with `point(name, fields)`. The engine loads it when the file is there.
6. **A listener never fails a run.** An error in the toast hook is caught, written to the log and returned once in the response, and the CLI prints it as one warning line. The run's outcome and exit code stay as they were.
7. **The CLI's own moments are not points.** The hs start, the deadline, a kill, and a refusal before the engine is asked are log records only. The engine is not running then, and Menuz's notice for a non-zero exit stays as the fallback. A failed engine run shows both the Finished toast and Menuz's notice (ic's call).
8. **Hands off.** From the first `step` to `finished`, arngz moves the pointer, and runs 106 and 113 lost moves to a hand on the mouse. From the first step, the Running toast says "Hands off the mouse and keyboard until it finishes." (ic's wording).
9. **Toasts are for apply** (ic's call). Every other verb answers inside one IPC call, so nothing can be drawn until it has answered. A Finished toast for discover (Save Desk...) is ic's open question to vc. The points still go out for every engine verb, so the log has them.
10. **A reload and its retry** (WP a45b3aeb). One CLI command is one run, so all its points carry one `run`. When a `finished` carries `reload`, the CLI asks the engine's `reload` verb, then its `state` verb until Hammerspoon answers from a fresh config, then the same verb once more. Each of these engine calls emits its own `start` and `finished` under that `run`, and rules 1 and 3 hold for each call. The retry's `start` carries `after_reload_of`, the same id. The toast draws nothing for `reload` and `state` (rule 9). The reload ends the Lua state, so the first run's Finished goes when the reload runs, and the retry's toast starts afresh. A reload refused, or a Hammerspoon not back in time, leaves the first Finished as the last toast, and the CLI's exit is not 0, so Menuz's notice carries the CLI's words (rule 7).
11. **A pause for the pointer** (WP 4cb617e2). When the person takes the pointer during a step, apply lets go and emits `waiting` for "the pointer to be still", with `seconds` 30 (how long it waits) and `still` 2 (how long the pointer must stay still). Once the pointer is still, the paused step goes out again, with the same `i` and `n`, and for a move with the window's frame as it is then, since the release left the window where it was. A pause that gives up sends no point of its own: the next `step` or `finished` follows. A run pauses at most 3 times, and `finished.paused` says how many times it did.
